narrator.instructions: Warm, confident corporate trainer speaking American English to colleagues. Clear, friendly, professional; natural conversational pace, brief pauses between list items. Never robotic.

narration.text: Welcome to Northwind. In the next three minutes, you'll learn how to submit an expense claim that gets paid the first time.

claims.text: This lesson covers submitting an expense claim at Northwind Co.

scenes.notes: Presenter: ask who has already paid for something work-related out of pocket. Time: 30 s.

narration.text: Here's why it matters. In twenty twenty-five, ^ eighteen percent of expense claims were sent back, because a receipt was missing. Claims with every receipt were paid in about six business days.

In 2025, claims submitted with all receipts were reimbursed in an average of 6 business days.

narration.text: Four rules come before anything else. ^ Keep an itemised receipt for every expense over twenty-five dollars. A card statement alone doesn't count. ^ Submit within thirty days of the expense. ^ After ninety days, a claim isn't paid at all. ^ And personal costs, like family meals, are never business expenses.

claims.text: A receipt is required for every expense over $25.
A card statement alone is not a receipt.
Employees must submit expense claims within 30 days of the expense date.
Claims older than 90 days are not reimbursed.
Personal costs such as family meals must not be submitted as business expenses.

scenes.notes: If asked about small items: no receipt needed at $25 or less, but keeping one never hurts.

narration.text: ^ When you travel, these limits apply. Meals are sixty dollars a day at home, and eighty-five dollars abroad. Hotels are capped at two hundred and twenty dollars a night, unless the Travel Desk approves an exception in writing. Flights under six hours are economy. And alcohol is only paid for client entertainment your manager approved in advance.

claims.text: The meal per diem is $60 per day for domestic travel and $85 per day for international travel.
Hotel costs are capped at $220 per night unless the Travel Desk approves an exception in writing.
Flights under 6 hours must be booked in economy class.
Alcohol is not reimbursable, except during client entertainment that the manager approved in advance.

scenes.notes: Example (SOP §8): Mona's pre-approved $140 client dinner incl. wine was reimbursed in full.

props.title: Six steps in the Northwind Expenses app

narration.text: Now, the claim itself, in six steps. ^ Photograph the receipt on the same day. ^ Open the Northwind Expenses app and select New Claim. ^ Choose the category, then enter the date, amount and business purpose. ^ Attach the receipt photo to each line, and check the total. ^ Submit it to your approver within thirty days. ^ And answer any question from your approver within five business days.

claims.text: Keep the itemised receipt for every expense and photograph it on the same day.
Open the Northwind Expenses app and select New Claim.
Choose the expense category and enter the date, amount and business purpose.
Attach the receipt photo to each line and check that the total matches.
Submit the claim to your approver before the 30-day deadline.
Respond to any approver question within 5 business days, or the claim is returned.

narration.text: Who approves depends on the amount. ^ You submit. ^ Your manager approves claims up to one thousand dollars. ^ A director approves up to five thousand. ^ And anything above five thousand goes to the C F O.

claims.text: A manager approves claims up to $1,000, a director up to $5,000, and the CFO any claim above $5,000.

narration.text: Quick check. Your conference trip comes to three thousand two hundred dollars. Who approves the claim?
^ A director. It's above one thousand dollars, but not above five thousand.

claims.text: A director approves claims up to $5,000; a manager approves claims up to $1,000.
Scenario: a $3,200 conference trip claim (fictional example).

narration.text: Three things you must never do. ^ Never split one expense into several claims to stay under a limit. ^ Never submit personal costs or private upgrades. ^ And never inflate a claim. False claims are treated as misconduct, and can lead to dismissal. Instead, ^ submit each expense once, with its real amount, ^ and ask Finance when you're unsure.

claims.text: Never split one expense into several claims to stay under an approval limit.
Do not submit personal costs, such as family meals or private travel upgrades, as business expenses.
Submitting a false or inflated claim is treated as misconduct and can lead to disciplinary action, including dismissal.
Questions about the policy go to the Finance Help Desk.
